title: Fine-grained token ledger with per-row sparklines and pricing pattern prototypes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a token-level cost analytics view that surfaces a compact, exportable ledger of token events with per-row micro-sparklines showing recent token usage, and a set of pricing UI patterns for viewing blended vs tiered costs. Focus on: 1) a schema for an exportable ledger (CSV/NDJSON/Parquet) that captures provenance (API key, route, model, quantization, cache hits, prompt slice), 2) a UI row pattern that includes a 48h sparkline, attribution badges, and expandable detail, 3) an interactive pricing comparison control that visualizes how different billing rules (flat per-token, tiered volume discounts, blended effective rates) change the bill, and 4) export UX for large datasets (sampling, progressive download, streaming NDJSON).
acceptance_criteria: Ledger export schema defined with column list and example row, including provenance columns: timestamp, request_id, api_key_id, route, model_version, prompt_slice_id, tokens_input, tokens_output, cache_hit, quantization_profile, unit_price, effective_price, cost_usd, annotations
Row UX mock includes compact sparkline, primary attribution chips (project, route, model), and an expand panel that shows token-level prompt/response length and kernel/runtime tag

Pricing patterns panel implements at least two visual modes: Blended effective rate (single metric) and Tiered breakdown (stacked bars by tier), with a dynamic slider to simulate commit/discount levels
Export modal supports CSV and NDJSON, with checkboxes to include optional columns, and a progressive export for datasets >1M rows with a streaming link
Prototype flows validated in 2 design reviews with eng and PM and action items captured
Security review note added for API-key-level exports and PII redaction guidance
design_notes: Primary goal is an engineer-friendly ledger that supports debugging, cost attribution, and chargeback. Avoid overwhelming the table with full prompt text by default: show prompt_slice_id and provide truncated preview with hover-to-expand. Sparklines are small (28x64) and show token volume over last 48 hours; clicking sparkline filters timeseries charts above. Attribution chips should be tappable and act as table filters. Pricing panel should show delta badges when switching patterns (e.g., +12.3% cost). For very large exports include a provenance header file and a minimal manifest containing model/quantization mapping. Quantization_profile should map to applied kernel and precision (e.g., q4_0 / int8).
review_feedback: PM (Lina Patel): Add clear default column set to avoid export confusion; only include full prompt text when 'include_prompt' checked.
Eng (Ravi Singh): Need to add request-level trace_id and ensure export respects retention TTLs; streaming NDJSON must be resumable.
Security (Ana Gomez): Flagged API-key-level exports; require scoped RBAC and an export audit trail. Must mask any user-provided PII by default.
Design (Jules Park): Sparklines look noisy with default sampling; add min/max smoothing and a hover tooltip with exact token count per bucket.
decisions: Default export columns will be the minimal safe set: timestamp, request_id, api_key_id (hashed), route, model_version, tokens_input, tokens_output, cache_hit, cost_usd
Full prompt text removed from default export; available via opt-in with explicit justification and audit logging
Sparklines implemented client-side with pre-aggregated 1-hour buckets from the metrics service to avoid heavy payloads
Pricing patterns panel will calculate blended effective_rate and also show tiered stacked bars; simulation slider runs client-only math and shows estimated monthly extrapolation
next_steps: Create engineering spike ticket to define server export job API and resumable NDJSON endpoints (ENG-XXXX)
Hand off annotated Figma frames to front-end with component spec and accessibility notes
Add a security checklist item to the Console export flow for RBAC checks and export audit entries
Schedule cross-functional review with Dedicated/Private product owners to validate export/retention limits
